title: Immunization Services Desk Training — The Resumed-Series Scheduling Allowance
content:
Patient Care Desk training, Immunization Services: the resumed-series allowance within Kestrel's scheduling allowance for a phone appointment for the next dose of a vaccination series.

> **Rule.** The resumed-series allowance is **1 day** where the course the series history is on was closed 60 days ago or less, **2 days** where it was closed more than 60 days ago, and nothing where it is not closed.

**Q. What makes the course "closed" for this rule?**
A. The course carries a closing date — it was completed or cancelled. A course in scheduled or in-progress status with no closing date is not closed, and the allowance is nothing.

**Q. How are the 60 days counted?**
A. In calendar days from the closing date to today, the closing date being day 0. A course closed today is 0 days ago.

**Q. What happens exactly on day 60?**
A. A course closed 60 days ago is "60 days ago or less": the allowance is 1 day. On day 61 it is "more than 60 days ago": the allowance is 2 days.

| Course the series history is on | Days since the closing date | Resumed-series allowance |
|---|---|---|
| not closed | not applicable | nothing |
| closed | 0 to 60 | 1 day |
| closed | 61 or more | 2 days |

**Worked cases (hypothetical).**

1. The course closed as completed 45 days ago: 45 is 60 or less, so the allowance is 1 day.
2. The course was cancelled 200 days ago: 200 is more than 60, so the allowance is 2 days.
3. The course is in progress with no closing date: the allowance is nothing.
